items.reply: I retain TP: writing each arriving span’s redirect does not flatten existing descendants when their root is subsequently re-parented. Separate bottom-up batches can create s0→s1→…→s1002; a later child of s0 resolves to s1001 under the new loop, whereas the previous limit reaches s1002. Eviction removes sorted-set payloads without shortening the redirect hash, so the 1000-span cap does not prevent this incorrect segment assignment. This is an uncommon-input correctness regression; an optimisation motive alone does not establish that it is intended behavior.
